long_biography.plain_text:
Geoffrey Pilkington's death in 1978 brought his 27-year-old son Jeremy into the family equipment-hire company, then known as Vibroplant. Three years later he became chair and chief executive of the listed business. During his first two decades, the group expanded through shoring, powered access, tool-hire and rail-equipment operations.

Vibroplant left general plant hire in 2000, adopted the Vp name and concentrated on higher-value specialist rental. Further acquisitions broadened the portfolio across trench support, temporary access, test equipment, tools and energy services. Pilkington later handed day-to-day management to a separate chief executive. He remains chair, providing governance and strategic oversight, while family-connected trusts control Vp's holding company.
